A:mary-dockery:newton.note: Mary Ann Dockery married Bailus Newton in 1867. The 1880 census records Balus Newton, wife Mary and a daughter Elizabeth, seven. Their identification with Lizzie Newton and her father Balas, named in the 1889 marriage papers, is probable; the census does not explicitly say Mary was Elizabeth’s mother. An Alabama death index names Mary Marzee Dockery as the mother of Oda Verbena Newton, a possible match for the youngest child in the household. Parents: Zilpha Etta Scott (proven) and William Dockery (very probable) (m. Spartanburg, S.C., 1818), from Zilpha's 1902 Dallas Morning News interview naming a twin daughter Mrs. B. Newton near Gadsden; the 1867 wedding was at a Gibson home (sister Frances Jane m. a Gibson, Samuel F. in family trees). Called Marzee: 'Mazzie' Dockray, 9, twin of Paralee, in Zilpha's 1850 Benton Co. household; 'Marzee Newton' on her 1914 widow's application. R36: alive 23 Jan 1930 at Gadsden Route 4 with son A. B. Newton (widow's reclassification; she gave birth 15 May 1844, Etowah Co., and father William Dockery). d. 1933 (joint stone with Balous, Old Harmony Baptist Church Cemetery; Find a Grave 6285484): probable.

A:john-satterfield-1766.note: His will (Warren Co., Ky., Will Book D, p. 262, proved 10 Nov 1847) names Ephraim among thirteen children; Ephraim's son Henry's 1861 death register names Ephraim and Rutha as parents, which ties the line (probable). The will names a wife Mary but does not say she was Ephraim's mother, so no mother link is added. John's own father is disputed and not entered.

A:ruth-knowles-satterfield.note: Married Ephraim Satterfield 12 Nov 1809, Warren Co., Ky. Henry Satterfield's Kentucky death register entry (24 Dec 1861) names his parents as Ephraim and 'Rutha' Satterfield. Her father Joshua Knowles's 1824 will names 'Ruth Saterfield' among his daughters. Both seen through WikiTree transcriptions (probable).

A:joshua-knowles.note: Will dated 11 Nov 1824, proved Oct 1832, names wife Jemima and daughter 'Ruth Saterfield'. Whether Jemima was Ruth's mother is not stated, so no mother is entered.

A:william-croasdale-newhey.dp: Newhey, Forest of Bowland, Yorkshire, England
A:william-croasdale-newhey.note: Buried at the Friends' burial ground of Settle Meeting. The Welcome Society reference work, Patterson's list of Quaker emigrants and the family genealogist Cleaver ('highly probable') make him father of the 1682 emigrant Thomas Croasdale; secondary sources only (probable). His father, possibly Henry Croasdale of Newhey, is a lead and is not linked.

A:elizabeth-croasdale-newhey.note: Wife of William Croasdale, buried beside him at Settle Meeting. Her maiden surname is often given as Hayhurst, but no original record names it, so it is left off her name here.

A:ellen-cowgill.note: Settle Monthly Meeting certificate of 7 June 1682 lists 'Ellen Cowgill widow & her children'; John Cowgill, who married Bridget Croasdale in 1693, is identified as her son by the Cowgill family studies (probable). Her husband's name and her maiden name are not documented.

xf1-001.note: Private in the North Carolina militia, discharged near Stono 2 Jul 1779 and at Frederick County, Maryland, 14 Jan 1782 (pension file S 31049, as summarized in Stuart's 1979 Garrison compilation). Married Esther Alexander 14 Mar 1786, Mecklenburg Co. His father is unresolved: two different John Garrisons are proposed and neither is proved. His sworn 1832 pension declaration, made at Hickory Grove, Warren County, Kentucky, gives him as 69 on 24 August last, so born 24 August 1763 (1762 elsewhere); he served under Capt. Thomas Beatty in the select militia of Frederick County, Maryland, and was at the battle of Stono. The pension names no father.

xf1-002.note: Named as 'Esther Garrison' in her father Hezekiah Alexander's will of 8 Aug 1796, with a daughter Caroline Garrison (American Monthly Magazine, Apr 1913, p. 188). Her husband's name, Samuel Garrison, comes from the Garrison family record. Birth is 23 or 28 September 1762 and death 1827 or 1829 in Stuart's text; WikiTree places her death in Coles County, Illinois, which the family record does not support.

xf1-003.note: Mecklenburg magistrate, patriot and elder of Sugar Creek church; will dated 8 Aug 1796. The link from his daughter Esther to John Milton Garrison is probable. His parents, James Alexander and Margaret McKnitt, are linked as probable on the strength of the Dictionary of North Carolina Biography; the Cecil County land and probate records have not been examined.

xf1-004.note: Married Hezekiah Alexander 12 Jun 1752 (Dictionary of North Carolina Biography). Named as his wife and executor in his 1796 will. Stuart gives her death as 17 May 1806 at 71; an earlier note on this site has 1805.

xf1-005.note: Eldest child in the Garrison family record; married William Ray in 1814. Named as 'dau. Caroline Garrison' in her grandfather Hezekiah Alexander's will of 8 Aug 1796.

xf1-006.note: Married Rebecca Lyle 10 Jun 1813, Warren Co., Ky.; moved to Morgan County, Alabama. Birth day is 8 or 18 February in Stuart's text.

xf1-008.note: Married Eliza Pogue 23 Jun 1829 and Chalia S. (Mitchell) Jones 10 Dec 1840. Birth day is 21 or 25 September in Stuart's text.

A:wt2-james-margaret-alexander:fm.note: Named as James Alexander's mother in the same Maryland legislature entry, which calls James's first wife Margaret 'a cousin of her husband' and names a stepmother, Abigail, without a surname. A:mary-sample:father.note: His will, dated 26 January 1769 in Mecklenburg County, names his wife Esther, his sons John, Joseph and William, his daughters Mary Alexander and Esther, and “Hez: Alexander my Son in law” as co-executor with Esther, and leaves ten pounds to his daughter Mary. Stuart's supplement gives the date as 17 January.
source_urls: Ancestry, North Carolina, Wills and Probate Records (coll. 9061), Mecklenburg Original Wills, William Sample, 1769, image 524

A:mary-sample:mother.note: William Sample's wife and co-executor, named Esther in his 1769 will. The will does not say whether the children were hers; Mary, born about 1734, needs a mother married by then, so Esther as Mary's mother is probable. Her maiden name is unknown.

A:john-c-shackleford.note: Probable father of John Morgan Shackleford: in 1870 his widow kept house in Coosa County, Alabama, with their son John, 7. He was a corporal in Co. B, 46th Alabama, and his widow Tinzy J. filed a claim on 29 Aug 1864 from Rockford, Coosa County.

A:tinsey-duke-shackleford.note: Probable mother of John Morgan Shackleford, who named his daughter Mary Tinsley for her. In 1870 she was a widow at McCords Beat, Coosa County, with son John, 7, and Edward Duke, 70. Her 1838 Carroll County, Georgia, marriage and 1873 death are leads.

xr7-001.note: His will, proved in Chester District in November 1844 (Book A1 p. 32, Apt. 89, Pkg. 1417), leaves property to 'my son Vincent Brown Tims' and to his wife Winifred. First known from a family transcription (Lucille Brown, via the Carolina Magic blog, 2013); the original, signed 20 Nov 1841, has since been read. Winifred is not shown to be Vincent's mother, so no mother is entered. Very probably the son Joseph named in the earlier Chester will of Joseph Tims (d. 16 Aug 1801) and Mary Glover, whose daughter Sarah Estes the same will names (Seltzer 1981; Tims Bible). The original 1841 will names sons Vincent Brown, Alford, John and Joseph T. and daughters Harriet Farrar, Elizabeth Wages(?) and Sarah Castles(?). A Joseph who was the son of Joseph (d. 1801) and Mary is proven living in Chester in 1827; that he is this testator is probable. Winifred was probably a later wife (about 39 in 1850), not Vincent's mother.

xr9-001.b: 2 Dec 1740s or 1750s (family Bible; year digit lost)
xr9-001.note: Son of Amos and Frances Tims and husband of Mary Glover in a Tims family Bible (Cemetery and Bible Records, vol. 5, 1954). Father of Sarah Tims Estes (1776-1849; Seltzer, Cary-Estes Genealogy, 1981) and of Amos Tims (1771-1867). The Chester will the family calls his first names sons Amos, John and Joseph and daughters Sarah Estes, Mary Carter, Frances Boyd and Elizabeth Tims. Probably the Joseph Tims who petitioned for South Carolina land on 6 Nov 1770 and was paid by indent in 1785 for militia provisions in 1781 (leads). His will, dated 26 Jul 1801 and probated 4 Sep 1801 (Chester, Will Book B p. 212), names his wife Mary, his sons Amos, John and Joseph (Joseph received all his land), and his daughters Sarah Estes, Mary Carter, Frances Boyd and Elizabeth Tims.

xr9-002.note: Wife of Joseph Tims in the Tims family Bible; named as Sarah Tims Estes's mother in Seltzer's Cary-Estes Genealogy (1981). Mother of Amos (1771) and Sarah (1776); probably also of the Joseph Tims who died in 1844. Wife and executrix in the 1801 will. The 1827 Court of Ordinary hearing calls her 'Mary Tims widow of Jos Tims' and names her son Joseph and daughter Elizabeth, Mrs. Brown. Glover is from the Bible only.

xr9-003.note: Son of Amos Tims the elder (born Northamptonshire, England, 1684; 'Senr.' in Lunenburg Co., Va., 1760; died 1766) and husband of Frances, in the Tims family Bible. Probably the Amos Tims granted 400 acres in 1774 in what became Union District, S.C., and paid by indent in 1785 for provisions and forage for Continental troops in 1781 (leads). Bible copy only; dates uncertain.

xr9-004.note: Wife of Amos Tims and mother of Joseph in the Tims family Bible. Maiden name unknown.

xr14-t2.dp: Buffalo Ford, Randolph County, North Carolina
xr14-t2.note: Named among the elder Hugh's brothers in Joseph Moffitt's 1853 letter; witness to William Moffitt's will, 1796; 'Morfit, Charles' next to 'Morfit, William' in Randolph Co., 1790. Birth from his family Bible (FamilySearch Memories 32050865) as transcribed on WikiTree Moffitt-194; death date from family trees (lead). Wife Mary Cox (b. 23 Sep 1756, d. 17 Oct 1819, per family trees). Named as Hugh's father in the 1798 Cane Creek certificate. His grandson Benjamin's 1920 obituary calls him 'a native of Londonderry, Ireland' (tradition).

xr14-t3.dp: Moffitt's Mills, Randolph County, North Carolina
xr14-t3.note: Son of Charles and Mary (Cox) Moffitt (Cox family outline, from Quaker records: m. Hannah Cox 15 Mar 1798). State senator for Randolph County, 1832-33 (Senate journal; 1913 Manual), very probably this Hugh rather than his son Hugh (1802-1868), who is 'Hugh Moffett Junior' in the 1830 census. Died 14 Jan 1838 ('Hugh Moffitt, Esq., an aged and very respectable citizen', Fayetteville Observer, 24 Jan 1838); intestate; Moffitt v. Lane (N.C. 1842). Second wife Margaret Needham (1792-1865). Proven son of Charles and Mary by the Cane Creek marriage certificate of 15th 3rd month 1798 (married Hannah, daughter of Thomas and Sarah Cox, at Holly Spring). Probably the Hugh Moffitt disowned by Cane Creek on 5 Sep 1812 'for purchasing and holding a black person in Slavery'. Elected Aug 1832, Moffitt 361, Jesse Bray 316 (Fayetteville Weekly Observer, 21 Aug 1832).

xr14-t4.note: Youngest son of Hugh and Margaret (Needham) Moffitt; died Thursday 22 Jan 1920 at Asheboro, buried at Franklinville (The Courier, Asheboro, 29 Jan 1920, p. 1). Married (1) Martitia Baldwin, 25 Nov 1862 (index); (2) Grizelle Bagley. Not the 1835 convention delegate (Benjamin Elliott).

xr22-001.note: Husband of Zilpha Etta Scott, m. Spartanburg, S.C., 1818; nine children (six sons, three daughters). Hired to haul Cherokee families west in the removal; died of swamp fever soon after returning, per Zilpha's 1902 interview. Probable father of Mary Ann (Dockery) Newton: Zilpha names a daughter Mrs. B. Newton near Gadsden. 1840 census, St. Clair Co., Ala., p. 227: Wm Dockery, 30-39, with wife 30-39, five boys and a girl, matching Zilpha's 1850 children. Son William J. was born about 1845, so the 'swamp fever soon after the removal' story places his death too early. PROVEN father of Mary Ann (Dockery) Newton: on her Widows Blank for Reclassification, 23 Jan 1930, she named her father William Dockery, dead, died in Etowah County (ADAH pension file of Balus Newton; image read R36).

xr22-002.note: Dallas Morning News interview, 17 Jan 1902: daughter of John Scott; raised in Spartanburg District from age three; m. William Dockery 1818; later m. John Diffy (d. after about a year) and resumed the name Dockery. Living children 1902: B. C. (Killeen), Samuel R. (Nolanville), Mrs. Jane Gibson (Pattonville), and twins Mrs. C. W. Driscell (Roxton) and Mrs. B. Newton (near Gadsden, Ala.). Portrait c.1901 (img/p/zilpha-scott-dockery-portrait-c1901.jpg). Mother of Mary Ann proven (1850 household; Marzee 1914). m. (2) John Diffy 24 Apr 1856, St. Clair Co. 1900: Pattonville area, grandmother in Samuel A. Gibson's home, 9 children/5 living. Died the night of 15 Jan 1903 (Dallas dispatch, 16 Jan). Age conflict: 35 in 1850; 30-39 in 1840.

xr22-003.note: Farmer; father of Zilpha Etta Scott Dockery by her own 1902 account; moved from Virginia to Spartanburg District, S.C., about 1799. Eleven children (three sons, eight daughters), among them Frances (Mrs. Daniel Gilbert). Known only from Zilpha's own 1902 account.

xr28-001.note: Father of Rebecca (Lyle) Garrison. m. 21 Jan 1792 his first cousin Sarah Chaney; Loudoun → Bedford Co., Va. → Warren Co., Ky., 1806, where he bought land. Nine children (Nancy Blackwell, Elizabeth Welch, Rebecca Garrison, Thomas H., William H., Sarah Welch, Mary Hinton, John W., Matilda Williams). Stuart, Supplement (1979); O. K. Lyle, Lyle Family (1912), p. 353.

xr28-002.note: Wife (and first cousin) of Manasseh Lyle, m. 21 Jan 1792; m. (2) George Wilson after 1810. Stuart spells the name Chemey once. Stuart, Supplement (1979); O. K. Lyle, Lyle Family (1912), p. 353.

xr28-003.note: Named as Manasseh Lyle's father by Stuart (1979) and as 'probably Thomas Lyle' by O. K. Lyle (1912), whose descendants' account gives him children Sarah (m. Luke Mayhew), Nancy (m. Moses Mayhew), James and Menasseh. No document seen; test in Loudoun Co., Va., records.

xr28-004.note: Nicholite from Delaware in the western Guilford colony (Carroll 1983); received with wife Rhoda and nine children by New Garden MM 31 Mar 1798; disowned 26 Apr 1806. Son-in-law of Noble Covey (Rowan will 26 Dec 1790). Will dated 14 Apr 1830 (original and Will Book C copy read in R36; the 2006 transcription's 5 Apr is wrong), written by Moses McCrary(?) at his direction, proved Feb Term 1846 (file 0911); names Matthew, James, 'my son Noble Shaw', Aaron, Drury & Rhoda Wood, James & Mary Morton, Robert & Betsy Nordyke and former son-in-law Jonathan Fisher; no wife. Trees' d. 14 Apr 1836 is probably the will date garbled; the heirs called him 'the late Benjamin Shaw' in Oct 1830.

xr28-005.note: Wife of Benjamin Shaw; received with him at New Garden MM 31 Mar 1798. Called the daughter of Noble Covey by Carroll (1983); her son Noble bears his name. Not named in Benjamin's 1830 will. Trees' b. 10 Mar 1764 and d. 24 Jul 1820 are unsourced. PROVEN daughter of Noble Covey: his Rowan will of 26 Dec 1790 calls Benjamin Shaw and 'Rhoda his wife' his son-in-law and daughter (R36, image read). Not named in her stepmother Mary Covey's 1799 will.

xr28-006.note: Nicholite of Caroline Co., Md.; signed the 1774 decision organizing the Nicholite Society; m. 1775 Mary (Pegg) Bicham of Kent Co., Del.; earlier wife Rachel (daughter Ann b. 1764); in Rowan Co., N.C., 1790. PROVEN father of Rhoda (Covey) Shaw: his Rowan will of 26 Dec 1790 (recorded Feb 1791; image read R36) names his wife Mary, 'Son in law & Daughter Benjamin Shaw & Rhoda his wife', Levi & Rebecca Buckingham and Newell & Sarah Sapp (executor); witnesses James and William Welborn. Widow Mary's Guilford will (21st 6th mo. 1799, proved Feb 1807) names stepdaughter Sarah Sapp and her Pegg brothers, not Rhoda. Carroll, Southern Friend 5:2 (1983).

xr26-001.note: Probable father of Balus Newton. m. Elizabeth West, Pendleton/Pickens District, S.C., 23 Nov 1831. Pickens Dist. 1840; Calhoun Co., Ala. (P.O. Peeks Hill) 1860; Etowah Co. (P.O. Gadsden) 1870, next township to Balus. Birth and death dates from Find a Grave 6287446 (Old Harmony Baptist Church Cemetery, Rainbow City), not checked against the stone.

xr26-002.note: Married Hezekiah Newton 23 Nov 1831 (Pendleton Messenger, 30 Nov 1831). Wife of Hezekiah, 46 in 1860 and 56 in 1870, so born about 1814. Probable mother of Balus; that the Elizabeth of 1860/1870 is the 1831 bride is probable, not proven.

xr38-001.note: Planter of Spotsylvania Co., Va., who signed with his mark. On 5 Aug 1746 he deeded to 'his daughter, Lydia Arnold' the plantation where her husband William Arnold lived, with 70 acres, and to his daughter Bathsheba Bell his own home place, with 100 acres, reserving a privilege to Lydia (Deed Book D, recorded 2 Sep 1746; Crozier p. 173). Bathsheba was the wife of Benjamin Arnold by 1760. The father-daughter tie is stated in the deed; the line to Catherine (Arnold) Payne is probable.

xr38-002.dp: St. George's Parish, Spotsylvania County, Virginia
xr38-002.note: Will dated 25 Jul 1764, executors' bond 20 Sep 1770 (Spotsylvania Will Book D, p. 421): wife Frances; sons John (eldest), Thomas, Barnett, William, Robert, George; unnamed daughters. Deed of gift to son Wm. Payn, 100 a., 4 Jun 1764. Proven father of the William Payne who married Catherine; probable 6th great-grandfather (depends on that William being William Paine of Burke Co.). Father Barnett Paine of Drysdale Par., King and Queen Co., is a lead only.

xr38-003.note: Wife of John Pain, joined him in deeds of 1745 and 1764 (including the 1764 gift to their son William) and his widow and life legatee in his 1764 will. Maiden name given as Coleman by family researchers (unsourced; John bought land from Robert and Thomas Coleman).

xr38-004.note: Wife of Henry Willis, with whom she sold land on Clifty and Fishing creeks, Pulaski Co., Ky., in 1800; on the Pulaski tax list alone by 1818. Traditionally the Mary Cochran named with a Henry Willis in a Fincastle Co., Va., grand-jury presentment of 1773. Lavina Willis Clark's mother only if Lavina was Henry's daughter, which is presumed, not shown.

xw7-001.note: Eldest of the eight Davies children in Boone's chart (born 9-28-1733, Friends' dating). Boone says he married Mary Chamness and, second, Elizabeth Jarvis. Hanson (1922) names the signer John Davis of the 1763 Chamness-Norton certificate as the man who married Mary Chamness. Which Chamness daughter Mary was is not read from a register here.

xw7-002.note: Second child in Boone's chart (born 1-18-1735, Friends' dating); she says he married Elizabeth Knox. Nothing else has been found.

xw7-003.note: Married Thomas Vestal (born 8 Sep 1727, Chester Co., Pa.; died 12 Jun 1813, Chatham Co., N.C.). Boone's Vestal chapter has the intentions declared 6 Jul 1754 at Cane Creek and the wedding on 7 Sep 1754; her Davies chart says the wedding was in Chester County. Ten children, the first born Oct 1755 in Orange County.

xw7-004.note: Boone gives her birth as 1739 and says she married Thomas Cox. The Cox outline shows Thomas Cox (born about 1736) marrying Sarah Davis, daughter of Charles and Hannah Davis, on 24 Jan 1760 in North Carolina; the scan of the table is rough.

xw7-005.note: Married Hugh Moffitt, a brother of William Moffitt according to Joseph Moffitt's letter of 1853 and the Bible record, as told in the story Six brothers from Donegal. Hugh's will of 1799 names his wife Hannah and son Joseph. Not to be confused with Hannah Cox, who married a later Hugh Moffitt in 1798.

xw7-006.note: Boone has her born 10-11-1748 in Orange County; the Cox outline has 11 Apr 1749. The outline shows her marrying a second Thomas Cox (born about 1740, died 14 May 1821) on 9 May 1771 at Cane Creek Meeting, and gives her death as 25 Aug 1829.

xw7-007.note: Youngest of the eight in Boone's chart (born 5-14-1751, Friends' dating). Boone says she married Abraham Osburn and, second, Owen Williams. Nothing else has been found.

xw7-008.note: Named in John Broad's will of 18 Sep 1702 as Thomas, son of John and Joanah Coal. Joseph Coale's will of 1720/1 names Thomas Coale and his wife Sarah as remainder heirs. Boyd (1935) calls him the eldest son, guardian in 1739 of the children of Aquilla Massey (who called him brother-in-law) and father of a Thomas Jr. who married Sarah Price in 1747.

xw7-009.note: Joseph Coale's will of 1720/1 names Charles Gorsuch and his heirs by his wife Sarah Coale. Boyd (1935) makes her John Cole's daughter and says John and Dinah Cole deeded a 100-acre tract, Bethel, to Charles Gorsuch. Not the Sarah Cole born in 1718 who married Anthony Chamness, who was probably her niece.

xw7-010.note: Wife of John Ensor, born 1695, according to Boyd (1935). The 1750 deposition of John Ensor Sr., aged 55, calls John Cole his father-in-law (as quoted in the story of John Cole). Boyd records a deed of 100 acres of Daniel's Whimsey from John Cole Sr. and Jr. to Ensor.

xw7-011.note: Grandson of Dennis and Barbara Garrett: named in Barbara Garrett Broad's deed of Aug 1712 (as quoted in the story of Sarah Cole) and listed by Boyd (1935) among John Cole's children by Johanna. Witnessed John Cole's will in 1745. His will, dated 1 Dec 1772 and proved 16 Jun 1773, is known only from Boyd's abstract.

xw7-012.bp: St. Paul's Parish, Baltimore County, Maryland
xw7-012.note: Daughter of Dennis Garrett Cole, named as deceased in his will with her six children. Boyd (1935) says she married John Mallonee (Malone), a Quaker, in 1748.

xw7-013.bp: St. Paul's Parish, Baltimore County, Maryland
xw7-013.note: Daughter of Dennis Garrett Cole, named in his will as wife of John Price. Boyd (1935) says she married John Price Jr. on 26 1mo 1753 (Gunpowder Meeting records) and was living in 1793.

xw7-014.note: Daughter of Dennis Garrett Cole, named in his will as wife of Stephen Gill, with a grandson Stephen Gill. Dates not found.

xw7-015.note: Named as son in John Broad's will of 18 Sep 1702 and under sixteen then. The Herring Run park history says he was about 17 when his father died in Jan 1709/10. Half-brother of Johanna Garrett Cole. That Barbara was his mother rests on the park history and Boyd (1935), supported by the 1712 deed that calls her Barbara Garrett Broad. Boyd says he married Ann Hawkins.

xw7-016.note: Named as daughter in John Broad's will of 18 Sep 1702, to be of age at twelve. The park history says she was about 13 in Jan 1709/10; Boyd (1935) calls her June and says she probably died young, which the park history contradicts.

xw8-001.note: The Bible's Amos Tims, Sen. Virginia records show an Amos Tims by 1717 (land granted 22 Jan 1717), in 1731/2 selling Nottoway River land in Surry County with his wife Elizabeth (signing by mark), with 200 acres in the 1727 Brunswick County land-grant index, on Lunenburg road crews in 1751 and 1757, and as 'Amos Tims, Senr.' in Lunenburg in 1760. Birthplace and death date are the Bible's only. The identification of the Virginia man with the Bible's man is probable.

xw8-002.note: Named as wife of Amos Tims in the Surry County deed of 18 Feb 1731 (old style), recorded 15 Mar 1731. Whether she was the mother of the younger Amos Tims (b. 1725 per the Bible) or a later wife is unknown; she is not linked as his mother. Maiden name unknown.

xw8-003.note: Father of Gov. Neill S. Brown, Gov. John C. Brown and, by three witnesses, of Margaret Caroline Brown Stevenson. Came from North Carolina to Giles County, Tennessee, in 1809 (Moore, 1923); farmed in the Bethany neighborhood about fifteen miles southeast of Pulaski. Dates are from Farrell (1946); a 1933 compendium appears to give 1780-1848 as well. Father possibly Angus Brown of Robeson County (lead, not linked). Not the Duncan Brown who died in Robeson County in January 1859, nor the minister Dr. Duncan Brown born 1771.

xw8-004.note: Married Duncan Brown 16 Jan 1805, per Farrell (1946); sister of Sarah Smith, who married Daniel McCallum. Mother of the two governors named Brown. Parents possibly Neill Smith and Mary Little of Robeson County (lead, not linked). Death date not found.

xw8-005.note: Per Farrell (1946): married about 1765 Mary McFarland; elder of Ashpole Presbyterian congregation (communicants' list of 16 Mar 1818); will written 1820, proved 1831, naming sons John and Duncan. Farrell lists Duncan Brown (b. 1780) as his son, but also notes that an earlier writer confused two Duncan Browns, and the will's Duncan may be a different man. Not linked.

xw8-006.note: Per Farrell (1946): married Mary Little in 1780; Revolutionary War voucher no. 4305 dated 27 Aug 1783 in the N.C. Treasurer's Office Papers (not opened). Listed as father of Margaret Smith (b. 1782), who married Duncan Brown. One compilation only; not linked.

xw8-007.note: Per Farrell (1946): wife of Neill Smith; died in Giles County, Tennessee. Farrell says the Little family's data come from two old family charts of about 1850 and are 'not otherwise substantiated.' Not linked.

xw8-008.note: Named by his son Rev. William Thomas Andrews in the 1912 autobiography in Memorial Sketches (p. 340) as his father; died 'as I am told, when I was about two years old.' No census or other record seen.

xw8-009.note: Named by her son Rev. William Thomas Andrews (1912) as his mother, born Eliza Ann Brown. Widowed with a large family in Limestone County, Alabama, she moved to Giles County, Tennessee, 'where most of her relatives lived and where she owned a good farm.' No tie to Duncan Brown's family is claimed.

xw8-010.bp: Burlington County, New Jersey (probably, per Boyd; Stafford County, Virginia, per Terrell)
xw8-010.note: Son of Abraham Nordyke and Mary Rogers by the family's Quaker certificates (via Hinshaw, Boyd, Terrell); married Charity Ellis at Lost Creek Monthly Meeting, Tenn., 4 Apr 1798; twelve children; to Ohio 1805/1806; buried East Fork Quaker Cemetery. Birthplace conflict: see the story.

xw8-011.note: Wife of Micajah Nordyke (m. 4 Apr 1798, Lost Creek Monthly Meeting); mother of twelve; daughter of Nehemiah Ellis and Sarah Thornbrough per Boyd (2009) and Terrell (1960). Buried East Fork Quaker Cemetery.

xw8-012.note: Quaker: from Exeter Monthly Meeting, Berks Co., Pa., to Hopewell Monthly Meeting, Va., 1773; married Sarah Thornbrough 10 Aug 1774 at Middle Creek; charter member of Lost Creek Monthly Meeting, Tenn., 17 Jun 1797; to Highland and Clinton counties, Ohio, 1812; buried Newberry Quaker Cemetery, Martinsville (per Boyd, 2009). Terrell's Mordecai Ellis of Wales is a lead only.

xw8-013.note: Wife of Nehemiah Ellis (m. 10 Aug 1774, Middle Creek); mother of Charity Ellis Nordyke per Boyd and Terrell; buried East Fork Quaker Cemetery, Green Township, Clinton Co., Ohio.

xw8-014.note: Named as 'Thomas, Amelia Co.' father of Cisley Elmore in the Cedar Creek marriage entry of 19 Nov 1758; two printed Quaker genealogies give his marriage to Cecilia Ellyson at New Kent County, Va., in 1729 (as Thomas Elmore Jr. in a 1963 book, III in a blogger's list). Birth and death dates are not established; online trees conflict. Residence: Amelia County, Virginia.
